Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates unilateral hyperlucency of the right hemithorax with diminished vascular markings (vessel paucity) and a smaller right hilum, which are classic features of Swyer–James–MacLeod syndrome (post-infectious obliterative bronchiolitis). This condition is strongly associated with a history of recurrent lung infections in childhood, making it the most clinically significant finding consistent with the provided context.
